messages:
jamie: Quick sync — need to decide an ownership model for service-to-service auth. Problem: many services are product-owned, some are infra-owned. Right now most API keys are org-scoped which makes least-privilege and audits hard.

sasha: Short options summary: (A) keep org-scoped keys + per-route RBAC enforcement; (B) move to project-scoped service keys + an operator broker for cross-project calls; (C) hybrid (project keys + org operator roles).

lee: Infra team leans toward B. Project-scoped keys are simpler to reason about and rotate. Broker handles cross-project delegation and short TTLs. :thumbsup:

morgan: Hybrid (C) is attractive for bootstrap: infra/shared routers keep org-level creds BUT they get tight ACLs + HSM-backed rotation. Product services get project keys.

jamie: Key tradeoffs I see: broker adds complexity and an availability surface. Org-scoped keys are simple but widen blast radius. Project-scoped + broker = better audibility and least-privilege, worse operational surface.

sasha: Prototype flow we discussed earlier:
```
svc-A (project X) -> broker -> svc-B (project Y)
broker mints ephemeral token TTL=60s with claims {iss:broker, sub:svc-A, to:project-Y, routes:[/v1/pay,/v1/alloc]}
```
This gives caller-limited rights.

lee: Agreed. Also enforce token size limits. If claims list gets long, use opaque token referencing a policy entry (broker stores policy id).

morgan: For infra-owned services: we must define a special 'operator' role with explicit minting permissions in IAM. Operator keys are short-lived too, bound to KMS/HSM, and rotate automatically.

jamie: Rollout proposal: 1) build broker v0 with opt-in, 2) pilot with two product teams + infra router, 3) require new product services to use project-scoped keys, 4) deprecate product use of org-scoped keys in 6 months.

sasha: Question: who enforces route-level policy — broker or callee? If broker embeds route whitelist in token, edge can reject earlier. If callee enforces, you get per-service fine-grained checks but extra latency.

lee: Prefer embedding minimal allowed scopes in token and let edge reject fast. Callee can double-check for sensitive paths.

morgan: That means tokens may carry more claims. To limit token bloat, we should prefer opaque reference tokens that map to stored policy in broker or an authoritative policy service.

jamie: Security ops notes: need audit trail for minting events, token lookups, and a clear incident path if broker is compromised (revoke policy id, rotate broker signing key).

deploy-bot: Heads-up: add feature-flag gating for broker rollout. Deploy to staging first and test key rotation flows.

sasha: Action items: @sasha write a mini-RFC capturing API shape, token formats (JWT vs opaque), error semantics, and rollout timeline. @lee draft broker SLOs and HA architecture. @morgan write infra key bootstrap and HSM rotation requirements. @jamie coordinate pilot teams.

jamie: Thanks — will schedule a short sync after the mini-RFC lands. End of thread. :white_check_mark:
